items.name: charts-ethereum
items.title: Ethereum Chart
items.description: A coin price card: the price with its change over the period, a Week / Month / Year switch, the NAV and market price with their changes, and green and red candles on a dashed price grid with the volume under them. Hover, drag or the arrow keys inspect a candle: the others fade back and a dark tooltip reads its time, change, open, high, low, close and volume. Animated with anime.js: the candles grow out of their opens one after another, and a new period morphs them into the new ones while the numbers count.

meta.docs:
A coin price card: the ETH coin and its name over the price with its change over the period, a Week / Month / Year switch, the NAV and the market price with their changes, and candles on a dashed price grid with the volume under them, green when the price closed at or above its open and red when it closed below. Hover (or drag on touch) along the candles: the others fade back, a dashed guide marks the candle, its day darkens on the axis and a dark tooltip reads its time, change, open, high, low, close and volume. Everything moves with anime.js: the coin spins in, the price and the badge count up, the figures and the period control come in, the grid draws across and the axes come in, then the candles grow out of their opens from left to right with their volume rising. A new period morphs the candles into the new ones (each new candle comes out of the old one at the same place, the old ones close in on theirs and fade) while the badge counts and the axes come in again; the tooltip pops in and slides from candle to candle.

## Usage

With the sample data (the Figma week: 77 candles from Monday to Sunday closing at $10,974.58, with a sample month of daily candles and a year of weekly ones that end at the same price):

```tsx
import { EthereumChart } from "@/components/ethereum-chart"

export function Example() {
  return <EthereumChart className="max-w-[600px]" />
}
```

With your own data:

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { EthCoin, EthereumChart, type EthereumCandle, type EthereumPeriod } from "@/components/ethereum-chart"

const DAY = 86_400_000
const start = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12) // Monday 12 October 2026

// one candle a day: [open, high, low, close, volume in ETH]
const days: [number, number, number, number, number][] = [
  [3412.5, 3468.2, 3380.1, 3441.8, 182400],
  [3441.8, 3502.6, 3420.4, 3488.9, 201300],
  [3488.9, 3511.3, 3402.7, 3418.2, 236800],
  [3418.2, 3436.9, 3351.5, 3366.4, 254100],
  [3366.4, 3429.8, 3340.2, 3415.7, 198600],
  [3415.7, 3480.1, 3398.5, 3472.3, 176900],
  [3472.3, 3495.4, 3448.6, 3459.1, 143200],
  [3459.1, 3530.7, 3451.2, 3524.6, 212700],
  [3524.6, 3588.4, 3510.9, 3571.2, 248300],
  [3571.2, 3602.5, 3519.8, 3533.4, 231500],
  [3533.4, 3547.6, 3462.3, 3478.9, 267900],
  [3478.9, 3521.4, 3466.1, 3509.8, 189400],
  [3509.8, 3556.2, 3497.3, 3549.1, 172600],
  [3549.1, 3573.8, 3528.4, 3512.4, 158100],
]
const candles: EthereumCandle[] = days.map(([open, high, low, close, volume], i) => ({ time: start + i * DAY, open, high, low, close, volume }))

const periods: EthereumPeriod[] = [
  { value: "week", label: "W", name: "Week", candles: candles.slice(-7), unit: "day" },
  { value: "two-weeks", label: "2W", name: "Two weeks", candles, unit: "week" },
]

export function Example() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = React.useState("week")

  return (
    <EthereumChart
      className="max-w-[600px]"
      title="Ethereum"
      icon={<EthCoin />}
      periods={periods}
      period={period}
      onPeriodChange={setPeriod}
      stats={[
        { label: "NAV", value: 3518.2, changeLabel: "NAV change", change: 24.6, color: "var(--primary-purple-500)" },
        { label: "Market price", value: 3512.4, changeLabel: "Market price change", change: -36.7, color: "#3a5eff" },
      ]}
      onInsightsClick={() => console.log("open the insights")}
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | `"Ethereum"` | Label/04 Semibold (truncates); also the card's accessible name. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` | `<EthCoin />` | The 28px coin before the title (the file exports `EthCoin`). |
| `symbol` | `string` | `"ETH"` | The unit of the volume in the tooltip ("2,700 ETH"). |
| `periods` | `EthereumPeriod[]` | `sampleEthereumPeriods` | One segment each: `{ value, label, name?, candles, unit }`. `candles` are `{ time, open, high, low, close, volume }` (time in ms), oldest first; `unit` is what the x axis names: `"day"`, `"week"` or `"month"`. With one period there is no switch. |
| `period` / `defaultPeriod` / `onPeriodChange` | `string` | the first period | Controlled or uncontrolled period. |
| `stats` | `EthereumStat[]` | `sampleEthereumStats` | The figures under the price, a column each: `{ label, value, changeLabel, change, color }`; `color` is any CSS colour for the swatches. `[]` hides them. |
| `formatTime` | `(time, context, unit) => string` | weekdays, dates, months | A time on the x axis (`"axis"`, "Mon") and in the tooltip (`"tooltip"`, "Mon, Oct 19, 2:11 AM"), in UTC by default. |
| `onInsightsClick` | `() => void` | – | Called by the sparkles button. |
| `locale` / `currency` | `string` | `"en-US"` / `"USD"` | Formatting of the prices, the figures, the axis ("$25K") and the times. |

Other props go to the card (`ChartCard`). The file also exports `EthCoin`, `sampleEthereumPeriods`, `sampleEthereumStats` and the types `EthereumChartProps`, `EthereumPeriod`, `EthereumCandle`, `EthereumStat` and `EthereumAxisUnit`.

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (600px in Figma) and the chart is drawn at the measured width; the height follows the content (562px). On a narrow card the period control wraps under the price and the figures stack in one column.
- The plot is 302px tall. The y axis has six round ticks that hold the period's highs and lows; the lowest tick is the plot's bottom edge (under the 1px Border/Sub axis), the highest the top dashed line, 7px down. The labels are spread over the plot's height, as in Figma, so the lower ones sit up to 7px above their lines.
- The candles are spread evenly from 7.09px in on the left to 7.73px in from the grid lines' right end (Figma's 6.55px spacing for 77 candles at 516px). Their bodies are 5px wide at that spacing and wider, up to 12px, when there are fewer; a body is at least 1px tall. Up candles are Primary/Green/green-500 with a green-600 inside stroke, down candles Error/error-500 with error-600, both with Figma's white inner shadow; the 1px wick runs from the high to the low.
- Each candle has its volume bar under it, as wide as its body and in its colour at 33.6%, scaled to the period's largest volume (42px).
- The price is the last close; the badge is the change from the first candle's open to it, in whole dollars: green with an arrow up, or red with an arrow down. The figures are shown as compact amounts with one decimal ("$11.0K", "-$836.5"), their labels in capitals; a change is red below zero and green above it.
- The x axis names each day, week or month centred under its candles, and leaves out a label that would run off the plot or into the one before it.
- The plot is a slider (one tab stop): the pointer, a drag on touch or the arrow keys pick a candle (Page Up / Page Down a tenth of the candles, Home / End the first and last), Escape hides the tooltip. The slider's text reads the candle's time and prices. The tooltip sits beside the candle, left of it near the right edge. The focus rings are blue.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing animates; the server render is the final state.
- The price, the badge and the figures are read from the candles (Figma's are placeholders), each candle has its own volume bar (Figma draws 63 bars under 77 candles), the last five candles keep the others' spacing and the days are centred under their candles: see FIGMA-GAPS.md.
- Figma: 1473:82288 ("Ethereum Chart", page "Home Frebies chart").

items.name: charts-category-breakdown
items.title: Category Breakdown Chart
items.description: A spending breakdown card: the month's revenue and expenses with their change from last month in badges, a Manage balance button, and the expenses as a meter of thin round ticks split among the categories, each starting with a tall tick under its name and share and shaded by its parts. Hover, drag or the arrow keys pick a part: its ticks rise, the other categories fade and a tooltip gives its amount and share; a click or Enter pins the category. Animated with anime.js: the figures count up, the ticks rise from left to right, the names come in as their ticks rise, and new amounts move the tall ticks and names while the ticks change colour.

meta.docs:
A spending breakdown card: the month's revenue and expenses side by side, each with its change from last month in a green (or red) badge, a "Manage balance" button, and the expenses as a meter of thin round ticks split among the categories. Each category starts with a tall tick under its name and share of the expenses, and its ticks are shaded by its parts, lightest first (Rent, Utilities and Repairs in Rent & Utilities). Hover, drag or arrow along the meter: the pointed-at part's ticks rise, the other categories fade and a dark tooltip gives the part's amount and share of the expenses; a click, a tap or Enter pins the category (again to unpin it). Everything moves with anime.js: the figures count up from zero and the badges pop, the divider draws in from the left, the ticks rise from the floor from left to right with each tall tick overshooting a little, and each category's name comes in as its tick rises while its share counts up. New amounts move the tall ticks (the old ones shrink, the new ones grow) and slide the names to their places while the ticks change colour and the numbers count; the tooltip fades in and glides from part to part.

## Usage

With the sample data (the Figma month: $18,645.16 of revenue and $6,364.81 of expenses over four categories of three parts each):

```tsx
import { CategoryBreakdownChart } from "@/components/category-breakdown-chart"

export function Example() {
  return <CategoryBreakdownChart className="max-w-[980px]" />
}
```

With your own data:

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { CategoryBreakdownChart, type CategoryBreakdownCategory } from "@/components/category-breakdown-chart"

const categories: CategoryBreakdownCategory[] = [
  {
    key: "housing",
    label: "Housing",
    color: "purple",
    items: [
      { label: "Mortgage", amount: 1840 },
      { label: "Energy", amount: 212.4 },
    ],
  },
  { key: "food", label: "Food", color: "orange", amount: 734.15 },
  { key: "transport", label: "Transport", color: "blue", amount: 298.6 },
  {
    key: "savings",
    label: "Savings",
    color: "green",
    items: [
      { label: "Pension", amount: 500 },
      { label: "Rainy day", amount: 250 },
      { label: "Travel", amount: 150 },
    ],
  },
]

export function Example() {
  const [category, setCategory] = React.useState<string | null>("food")

  return (
    <CategoryBreakdownChart
      className="max-w-[980px]"
      revenue={5120}
      previousRevenue={4980.5}
      previousExpenses={4102.33}
      categories={categories}
      category={category}
      onCategoryChange={setCategory}
      changeLabel="vs October"
      manageLabel="Budget settings"
      onManageClick={() => console.log("open the budget settings")}
      locale="en-GB"
      currency="GBP"
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | `"Category Breakdown"` | The card's accessible name (the card shows no title). |
| `revenueLabel` / `revenue` | `string` / `number` | `"Total revenue"` / `18645.16` | The first figure. |
| `previousRevenue` | `number` | `17008.43` | Last month's revenue: the first badge shows the change from it (left out without one). |
| `expensesLabel` | `string` | `"Monthly expenses"` | The label over the second figure, the sum of the categories. |
| `previousExpenses` | `number` | `6021.37` | Last month's expenses: the second badge shows the change from them. |
| `changeLabel` | `string` | `"This month"` | The soft text after the badges. |
| `categories` | `CategoryBreakdownCategory[]` | `sampleCategoryBreakdownCategories` | The meter, in order: `{ key, label, amount?, color?, items? }`. `amount` is the sum of the `items` when left out. `color` is `"purple"`, `"blue"`, `"orange"`, `"green"` or `"yellow"` (in turn by default). `items` (`{ label, amount }`) split the category's ticks by their amounts, each in its own shade, lightest first; a category without items fades through three shades in thirds. |
| `category` / `defaultCategory` / `onCategoryChange` | `string \| null` | `null` | Controlled or uncontrolled pinned category (by `key`): its ticks stay lit while the others fade. |
| `manageLabel` / `onManageClick` | `string` / `() => void` | `"Manage balance"` / – | The button beside the figures and what it does. |
| `locale` / `currency` | `string` | `"en-US"` / `"USD"` | Formatting of the amounts and the percentages. |

Other props go to the card (`ChartCard`). The file also exports `sampleCategoryBreakdownCategories` and the types `CategoryBreakdownChartProps`, `CategoryBreakdownCategory`, `CategoryBreakdownItem` and `CategoryBreakdownColor`.

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (980px in Figma) and the meter is drawn at the measured width; the height follows the content (305px). The meter is 124px tall: as many ticks as keep Figma's 8.68px pitch (109 over 940px), each 3px of colour in a 1px ring of the same colour with round ends, its core lit 19% white by Figma's inner shadow. A category's first tick runs the meter's height, the others are 72px, standing on its bottom edge.
- Each tick stands for an equal share of the expenses: a category gets the ticks its share covers (cumulative shares rounded, at least one while there are enough), and its items split them the same way. Three items take the colour's 100, 300 and 500 steps, two the 300 and 500 steps, one the 500 step. The shares over the meter are whole percents that add up to 100.
- A category's name and share start 8px right of its tall tick and are cut short (or hidden) before the next one. On a card narrower than about 650px the button wraps under the figures, under about 460px the figures stack.
- The badges show the change from last month in whole dollars, as Figma writes them: green with arrow-circle-up, or red with arrow-circle-down when the figure fell (a rise in spending is green too).
- The meter is a slider over the parts (one tab stop): the pointer, a drag or the arrow keys (Home, End) pick a part and show its tooltip, Enter or Space pins its category (again to unpin it), Escape lets go of both. The focus rings are blue.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing animates; the server render is the final state.
- The shares and the badges are read from the data (32%, 24%, 20% and 24% for Figma's 50%, 28%, 22% and 22%; +$1,637 and +$343 for Figma's $163,747), the shades are read as each category's parts and every share sits 4px under its name: see FIGMA-GAPS.md.
- Figma: 1473:77602 ("Category Breakdown Chart", page "Home Frebies chart").

items.name: charts-financial-trends
items.title: Financial Trends Chart
items.description: A cash flow card drawn as a dot matrix: the period's total net cash flow with a Week / Month / Year control over a grid of squares, one column per stretch of time and every square an equal amount, the money out stacked in blue from the bottom and the money in grey on top. A dashed line marks the selected column and a tooltip gives its dates and both amounts; the legend items take a series off the grid. Hover, drag or the arrow keys pick a column. Animated with anime.js: the matrix ripples in, the squares light up column by column while the total counts up, then the line runs down and the tooltip pops in; a new period slides the columns into place and recolours the squares that change.

meta.docs:
A cash flow card drawn as a dot matrix: the period's total net cash flow with a Week / Month / Year control over a grid of squares, one column per stretch of time and every square an equal amount: blue squares for the money that went out stacked from the bottom, grey ones for what came in on top, on a $ axis. A dashed line marks the selected column and a tooltip gives its dates and both amounts. The legend items take a series off the grid (hovering one brings its squares forward), hover or drag previews a column, a click or the arrow keys select one. Everything moves with anime.js: the matrix ripples in, the squares light up column by column from the bottom while the total counts up, then the marker line runs down and the tooltip pops in with its amounts counting; a new column slides the line and the tooltip over, and a new period or series slides the columns into place and recolours the squares that change, bottom up.

## Usage

With the sample data (the Figma content: 2026 in 32 stretches with 17 to 28 May selected, plus December by day and its last full week by six hours):

```tsx
import { FinancialTrendsChart } from "@/components/financial-trends-chart"

export function Example() {
  return <FinancialTrendsChart className="max-w-[560px]" />
}
```

With your own data:

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { FinancialTrendsChart, type FinancialTrendsPeriod } from "@/components/financial-trends-chart"

// one column per bucket: its start (an ISO date or date-time, UTC) and the money in and out over it
const weeks = Array.from({ length: 26 }, (_, i) => ({
  date: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 5) + i * 7 * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
  inflow: 8200 + ((i * 1370) % 3900),
  outflow: 5100 + ((i * 2210) % 4300),
}))
const months = ["2025-07-01", "2025-08-01", "2025-09-01", "2025-10-01", "2025-11-01", "2025-12-01"].map((date, i) => ({
  date,
  inflow: [38200, 41150, 39870, 44320, 47010, 52480][i],
  outflow: [31840, 35210, 33960, 36120, 38870, 46350][i],
}))

const periods: FinancialTrendsPeriod[] = [
  { value: "weeks", label: "Weekly", data: weeks },
  { value: "months", label: "Monthly", data: months },
]

export function Example() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = React.useState("weeks")

  return (
    <FinancialTrendsChart
      className="max-w-[560px]"
      title="Studio cash flow"
      periods={periods}
      period={period}
      onPeriodChange={setPeriod}
      onIndexChange={(index, bucket) => console.log(index, bucket.date)}
      onMoreClick={() => console.log("open the card menu")}
      locale="en-GB"
      currency="GBP"
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | `"Financial Trends"` | Heading/01 Semibold; also the card's accessible name. |
| `totalLabel` | `string` | `"Total net cash flow"` | The label over the big number: the period's money in minus money out. |
| `inflowLabel` / `outflowLabel` | `string` | `"Cash inflow"` / `"Cash outflow"` | The series' names in the legend and the tooltip. |
| `periods` | `FinancialTrendsPeriod[]` | `sampleFinancialTrendsPeriods` | The control's segments: `{ value, label, data }`, `data` one column per bucket, oldest first. A bucket is `{ date, end?, inflow, outflow }`: `date` is where it starts (an ISO date or date-time, UTC) and `end` where it ends (exclusive; the next bucket's date by default, the last bucket as long as the one before). With one period the control is left out. |
| `period` / `defaultPeriod` / `onPeriodChange` | `string` | `"year"` (sample), else the first | The shown period, controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `index` / `defaultIndex` / `onIndexChange` | `number` | the 13th column (sample), else the latest | The selected column (an index into the period's data); `onIndexChange(index, bucket)` runs on click, the keys and a period change. |
| `hiddenSeries` / `defaultHiddenSeries` / `onHiddenSeriesChange` | `("inflow" \| "outflow")[]` | `[]` | The series taken off the grid, controlled or uncontrolled; each legend item toggles its own (one always stays). |
| `formatSpan` | `(start: number, end: number) => string` | see below | The tooltip's first line for a bucket (ms, the end exclusive). |
| `onMoreClick` | `() => void` | – | Called by the ⋯ button. |
| `locale` / `currency` | `string` | `"en-US"` / `"USD"` | Formatting of every amount, the axis ("$50K") and the dates. |

Other props go to the card (`ChartCard`). The file also exports `sampleFinancialTrendsPeriods` and the types `FinancialTrendsChartProps`, `FinancialTrendsPeriod`, `FinancialTrendsBucket` and `FinancialTrendsSeries`.

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (560px in Figma) and the grid is drawn at the measured width; the height follows the content (472px). The grid has 15 rows of 12px squares 3px apart (222px). Its columns are spread from edge to edge, 12px wide while there is room for 3px between them (32 columns at Figma's 477px plot), narrower when there isn't.
- Every square stands for an equal amount: the axis' top over the 15 rows ($3,333.33 on the sample's $0–$50K axis). A column is its outflow in squares from the bottom, then its inflow on top, each rounded at its edge of the stack, so the column's height is its total. The axis runs from $0 to a round top that holds the tallest column (1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8 × 10ⁿ a step), one label every three rows, each centred on the gap where its value is reached; $0 and the top are kept inside the plot. Amounts below zero count as 0.
- The x axis follows the buckets' time span: month names over a long period, a date every few days over a few weeks, weekday names over a week, each centred on its stretch of the axis (a column's slot spans its bucket). The tooltip names the bucket: a calendar month "May 2026", a day "Tue, Dec 22, 2026", part of a day "Tue, Dec 22, 6 AM – 12 PM", several days "May 17 – 28, 2026".
- The marker line is Figma's dashed 1px line (4/4, fitted to the plot with half a dash at each end) fading from 2% at the ends to #171717 in the middle. The tooltip sits 10px right of it, or left of it near the end of the plot, its top 18px over the column's highest square (its date row level with it), kept inside the plot; it lists the shown series.
- The big number adds up money in minus money out over the period's buckets (both series, also while one is hidden).
- The grid is a slider: one tab stop. The arrow keys move the selection one column (Page Up / Page Down an eighth of the columns, Home / End the first and last). A new period keeps the selected moment when it covers it, else selects its latest column. The legend items are toggle buttons (pressed while their series is shown); hovering or focusing one fades the other series' squares. Focus rings are blue.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing animates; the server render is the final state.
- The sample opens on Year (Figma's January to December, where its control says Week), keeps Figma's total and reads the tooltip from the selected column; the y labels sit on their values and the month names under their months: see FIGMA-GAPS.md.
- Figma: 1473:84375 ("Financial Trends Chart", page "Home Frebies chart").

items.name: charts-asset-allocation
items.title: Asset Allocation Chart
items.description: An asset allocation card: the amount allocated and the portfolio's total next to a two-column flow chart in which bands carry the money from the classes it leaves to the classes it joins, labelled with each amount and its share, and a dark tooltip on the selected band with its share of both classes. Hover, focus or click a band to raise it with its tooltip, hover a class to light its bands, and switch classes off in the legend to reflow the chart. Animated with anime.js.

meta.docs:
An asset allocation card: how a portfolio moves between asset classes, as a two-column flow chart. The bars on the left are the classes the money leaves, the bars on the right the classes it goes to, each with its share of the whole; a band joins them for every amount that moves, labelled with the amount where it leaves and its share of the class it joins. The selected band is raised over the others with a dark tooltip: its share of the class it leaves ("Reductions"), the amount and its share of the class it joins ("Additions"). Next to the chart sit the amount allocated and the portfolio's total, over a legend that switches classes off and on. Everything moves with anime.js: the tile pops, the figures count up, the left bars grow, the bands flow in from the left on a soft edge into the right bars while every share counts up, the labels follow and the tooltip pops in; another band slides the tooltip over while its numbers count, and switching a class off or on morphs every band and bar to the new layout while the shares and the figures count.

## Usage

With the sample data (the Figma content: Equities and Cash Equivalents moving into Fixed Income, Real estate and Commodities, Equities → Real estate selected):

```tsx
import { AssetAllocationChart } from "@/components/asset-allocation-chart"

export function Example() {
  return <AssetAllocationChart className="max-w-[880px]" />
}
```

With your own data:

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { AssetAllocationChart, type AssetAllocationClass, type AssetAllocationFlow } from "@/components/asset-allocation-chart"

// the legend lists the classes in this order, and each column stacks its own classes in it
const classes: AssetAllocationClass[] = [
  { key: "stocks", label: "Stocks", color: "blue-light", side: "from" },
  { key: "bonds", label: "Bonds", color: "orange-light", side: "from" },
  { key: "index-funds", label: "Index funds", color: "blue", side: "to" },
  { key: "reits", label: "REITs", color: "orange", side: "to" },
  { key: "gold", label: "Gold", color: "yellow", side: "to" },
]

// in money; at every class the bands stack in this order, top to bottom
const flows: AssetAllocationFlow[] = [
  { from: "stocks", to: "index-funds", value: 42_500_000 },
  { from: "stocks", to: "reits", value: 18_250_000 },
  { from: "bonds", to: "reits", value: 9_800_000 },
  { from: "bonds", to: "gold", value: 6_400_000 },
]

export function Example() {
  const [hidden, setHidden] = React.useState<string[]>([])
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState<number | null>(0)

  return (
    <AssetAllocationChart
      className="max-w-[880px]"
      title="Rebalancing plan"
      description="What moves where this quarter"
      classes={classes}
      flows={flows}
      total={92_000_000}
      hiddenClasses={hidden}
      onHiddenClassesChange={setHidden}
      index={index}
      onIndexChange={(next) => setIndex(next)}
      onMoreClick={() => console.log("open the card menu")}
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | `"Asset allocation"` | Heading/01 Semibold; also the card's accessible name. |
| `unit` | `string` | the amounts' unit (`"$M"`) | The soft text after " / " in the title; by default the currency and compact suffix of the largest band ("$M", "€K"). |
| `description` | `string` | `"Strategic asset allocation approach to optimize portfolio distribution"` | Label/03 Medium in Text/Soft under the title. |

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (880px in Figma) and 472px tall. The chart is 352px tall, between two 72px columns of 60px bars; the bands stretch across the width left between them. On a card too narrow for both (under about 720px) the chart drops under the figures.

A bar is as tall as its bands and the gaps between them. A class without bands (switched off, or left without any) leaves the chart.

Bands thinner than 14px show their labels only while they are active. A bar shows its share of its column (hidden on bars shorter than 30px). Shares are whole percents that add up to 100 in every column and at every class.
- The bands are painted top to bottom by where they leave, the active one last; a band crossing one painted before it casts a soft shadow on it. The tooltip is centred over the bands, its bottom 18px above the active band's middle there (under it near the top).
- The amounts are the bands' buttons: Tab reaches the selected band, the arrow keys walk the bands top to bottom (Home / End jump), Enter selects and Escape lets go. Hovering or focusing a band raises it with its tooltip while the other bands, and the bars it doesn't join, fade back. Hovering a bar or a legend item lights the bands of its class. An asset overview card: a Week / Month / Year switch, the period's totals of two series (Mutual Funds and Stocks) and a stacked bar per slot of the period, blue funds under an orange stocks cap, with the days (weeks, months) named under the bars, an insight line and a "See insight" button. With the sample data (the Figma content: Monday 19 to Saturday 24 October 2026 in 39 slots, plus generated Month and Year periods):

  { key: "etf", label: "ETFs", color: "blue" },
  { key: "crypto", label: "Crypto", color: "orange" },
]

const periods: AssetOverviewPeriod[] = [
  {
    value: "week",
    label: "Week",
    // one bar per day: each tick sits under its bar
    ticks: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],

      { label: "Tue, Jun 2", values: { etf: 1240.5, crypto: 310 } },
      { label: "Wed, Jun 3", values: { etf: 640, crypto: 95.25 } },

      { label: "Fri, Jun 5", values: { etf: 980, crypto: 260 } },
      { label: "Sat, Jun 6", values: { crypto: 180 } },
      { label: "Sun, Jun 7", values: { crypto: 75 } },
    ],

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (414px in Figma) and the bars are drawn at the measured width; the height follows the content (497px with a one-line insight). The bars are equal, 2px apart, and stand on the plot's bottom edge; the tallest stack of the shown series is as tall as the plot (119px). An expenses card: the period's total with its change against the previous period in a green (or red) badge, a Week / Month / Year switch, a row per category with its amount, and a donut of the categories on the period's budget: Debt, Investment and Asset in orange, green and yellow, clockwise from 12 o'clock, each with a 1px rim, a soft inner light and (orange and green) a darker core, and what is left of the budget hatched in pale orange inside an orange outline. ## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | `"Expenses"` | Heading/01 Semibold; also the card's accessible name. |
| `totalLabel` | `string` | `"Total Expenses"` | Over the total. |
| `remainingLabel` | `string` | `"Left to spend"` | The hatched part's name in the middle of the ring. |
| `categories` | `ExpensesCategory[]` | `sampleExpensesCategories` | The segments, clockwise from 12 o'clock, and the rows: `{ id, label, color? }`. `color` is `"orange"`, `"green"`, `"yellow"`, `"blue"` or `"purple"` (the segment's 400 step with a 500 rim and, except yellow, a 600 core); by default the categories take them in that order. |
| `periods` | `ExpensesPeriod[]` | `sampleExpensesPeriods` | One segment each (the control hides with a single period): `{ value, label, values, budget?, previous?, changeLabel? }`, see below. |

| `locale` / `currency` | `string` | `"en-US"` / `"USD"` | Formatting of every amount and percentage. |

Other props go to the card (`ChartCard`). The file also exports `sampleExpensesCategories`, `sampleExpensesPeriods` and the types `ExpensesChartProps`, `ExpensesCategory`, `ExpensesPeriod` and `ExpensesColor`.

## Notes

- The card is as wide as its container (720px in Figma) and its height follows the content (502px). - A segment has Figma's effects: a 1px rim of its 500 step past its outer edge (Figma's spread scales the arc, so the rim only shows outside), a white inner light at 32% (blur 6, spread 2: strong along the outer edge, faint along the inner one, none along the ends, as Figma renders it) and, for every colour but yellow, a core in its 600 step blurred over the segment's middle and darkening it (with a soft halo around the ring). The hatched part is Primary/Orange/orange-50 bars 1.8° wide every 3°, ending at 12 o'clock, in a 1px orange-300 outline that runs on under the segments beside it.
- The rows are buttons in the tab order: Enter or Space holds a category, again lets it go; the focus ring takes the category's colour. Each row reads its label and amount, and the ring's label lists every category with its share and what is left of the budget. Pointers preview what is under them: a segment, a row or the hatched part.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing animates; the server render is the final state.

meta.docs:
The round legend swatch of the Keitoto chart cards, the circle beside ChartLegendSwatch's square: 14px, a 1px ring, a soft drop shadow, a faint inner shadow along the bottom and a 1px white inside stroke that fades out downward. `size={12}` is the dot scaled to 12px with everything on it (a 0.86px ring and stroke, smaller shadows), as the Profit Margin Analysis, Revenue Growth and Revenue by Product Line legends draw it. Set the fill with a background class and the ring with the `--dot-ring` CSS variable. ## Usage ```tsx import { ChartLegendDot } from "@/components/ui/chart-legend-dot" export function Example() { return (

Gross margin Net margin

items.name: charts-menu
items.title: Chart Menu
items.description: A small dropdown for the chart cards' period buttons (Weekly / Monthly / Yearly): Radix DropdownMenu with radio items, a check on the selected one and an anime.js scale-in.

meta.docs:
A small menu for the chart cards' period buttons ("Monthly ▾"), built on Radix DropdownMenu: radio items with a check on the selected one, opening with an anime.js scale-in. Keitoto doesn't draw the open menu, so it borrows the Segment Control's white surface, #ececec ring and soft shadow, with Label/02 text.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { ChevronDownIcon } from "@/components/ui/chart-icons"
import { ChartMenu, ChartMenuContent, ChartMenuRadioGroup, ChartMenuRadioItem, ChartMenuTrigger } from "@/components/ui/chart-menu"

const options = ["Weekly", "Monthly", "Yearly"]

export function Example() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = React.useState("Monthly")

  return (
    <ChartMenu>
      <ChartMenuTrigger className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-xl bg-surface-disable px-2.5 py-2 typo-label-03-medium text-fg-normal">
        {period}
        <ChevronDownIcon className="text-fg-soft" />
      </ChartMenuTrigger>
      <ChartMenuContent>
        <ChartMenuRadioGroup value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod}>
          {options.map((option) => (
            <ChartMenuRadioItem key={option} value={option}>
              {option}
            </ChartMenuRadioItem>
          ))}
        </ChartMenuRadioGroup>
      </ChartMenuContent>
    </ChartMenu>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Part | Props | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ChartMenu` | Radix `DropdownMenu.Root` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`. |
| `ChartMenuTrigger` | Radix `DropdownMenu.Trigger` | Unstyled: style your button; `data-state="open"` while open. |
| `ChartMenuContent` | Radix `DropdownMenu.Content` + `container` | Defaults `align="end"`, `sideOffset={8}`. Portals to `<body>` (or `container`) and carries `data-charts`, so the chart tokens apply there too. |
| `ChartMenuRadioGroup` | Radix `DropdownMenu.RadioGroup` | `value`, `onValueChange`. |
| `ChartMenuRadioItem` | Radix `DropdownMenu.RadioItem` | Label/02 Medium Text/Normal; highlighted Background/Disable; checked Text/Loud with a check. |

## Notes

- Keyboard and focus come from Radix (arrow keys, type-ahead, Escape, focus back to the trigger).
- With reduced motion the menu appears without the scale-in.
- Figma: the period button "Monthly Label" 1473:84272 in the Total Expenses card (the open menu is not drawn).

items.name: charts-segmented-control
items.title: Chart Segmented Control
items.description: The Keitoto Segment Control (Week / Month / Year): default or rounded, text or icon segments, a white thumb that slides to the selected segment with anime.js.

meta.docs:
The Keitoto "Segment Control": a row of segments with exactly one selected, marked by a white thumb that slides to it with anime.js. `variant="default"` is the 14px-cornered grey track with soft labels (Week / Month / Year on the chart cards); `variant="rounded"` is the pill track with darker labels. `size="icon"` gives 56px icon segments and a control that hugs them (the Column / Line switch). Arrow keys move between segments.

## Usage

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"

import { ChartSegmentedControl } from "@/components/ui/chart-segmented-control"

export function Example() {
  const [range, setRange] = React.useState("week")

  return (
    <ChartSegmentedControl
      aria-label="Range"
      className="w-[408px]"
      value={range}
      onValueChange={setRange}
      items={[
        { value: "week", label: "Week" },
        { value: "month", label: "Month" },
        { value: "year", label: "Year" },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

Rounded, with icon segments:

```tsx
import { ChartSegmentedControl } from "@/components/ui/chart-segmented-control"
import { CoinsStackedIcon, WalletSolidIcon } from "@/components/ui/chart-icons"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ChartSegmentedControl
      aria-label="View"
      variant="rounded"
      size="icon"
      defaultValue="wallet"
      items={[
        { value: "wallet", label: <WalletSolidIcon className="size-4" />, "aria-label": "Wallets" },
        { value: "coins", label: <CoinsStackedIcon className="size-4" />, "aria-label": "Investments" },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `{ value: string; label: React.ReactNode; "aria-label"?: string; disabled?: boolean }[]` | – | One segment each. Give icon labels an `aria-label`. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` | `string` | first item | Controlled or uncontrolled. Clicking the selected segment keeps it selected. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "rounded"` | `"default"` | Figma Type. Also `data-variant`. |
| `size` | `"text" \| "icon" \| "fit"` | `"text"` | Figma State: text segments share the width (the control is as wide as its container), icon segments are 56px, `"fit"` segments hug their labels (16px padding, whole-pixel widths) and the control hugs them (the Week / Month / Year and ETH / BTC switches of the Price Range card). |

Other props go to the root (`role="group"`); pass an `aria-label`.

## Notes

- Built on Radix `ToggleGroup` (single): roving focus, arrow keys, Home / End. The selected label is Semibold Text/Loud, the others Medium Text/Soft (Text/Normal on rounded); unselected labels darken on hover (not drawn in Figma).
- The thumb is positioned with CSS, so the server render is already right; with reduced motion it jumps instead of sliding. With `size="fit"` each segment holds its own thumb, and a change slides and stretches the new one over from the old segment.
- Figma: Segment Control 79:21365 (Keitoto library), used in the Total Value card as 1473:74757.

items.name: charts-tooltip-lines
items.title: Chart Tooltip Lines
items.description: The text of the Keitoto chart tooltips: the dark tooltip's two lines (the label in Text/Disable over the value in white), and the label and value on their own for the dark or the light (white) tooltip.

meta.docs:
The text of the Keitoto chart tooltips. `ChartTooltipLines` is the dark tooltip's two lines: the label (a date, a name) in Label/02 Regular, Text/Disable, over the value in Label/03 Medium, white. `ChartTooltipLabel` and `ChartTooltipValue` are those two lines on their own, for the dark tooltip or, with `variant="light"`, the white one (Text/Soft and Text/Loud). They are the text only: the tooltip's box, its place and its motion stay with the chart. ## Usage ```tsx import { ChartTooltipLabel, ChartTooltipLines, ChartTooltipValue } from "@/components/ui/chart-tooltip-lines" export function Example() { return (
{/* the dark tooltip: the label over the value */}
{/* the white tooltip: the value beside its label */}
$4,250.00 Income
) } ``` ## Props `ChartTooltipLines` takes `label` and `value` (any React node) and `valueRef`, a ref to the value's `` (for `useCountUp`). It renders the two spans with no wrapper, so they sit in the tooltip's own column (`flex flex-col items-start gap-2`). `ChartTooltipLabel` and `ChartTooltipValue` take every `` prop (`ref` too) plus `variant`: `"dark"` (the default) or `"light"`. Their data-slots are `chart-tooltip-label` and `chart-tooltip-value`. ## Notes - A tooltip whose value counts renders the lines twice: with `valueRef` in the tooltip, where the count writes each frame, and with the final text in an invisible copy (`invisible absolute`) that is measured to place the tooltip, since the counting value changes width. - The text boxes round up to whole pixels (`hug-w`) like Figma's hug width, so the measured copy is as wide as Figma's tooltip. - No hooks: use it from Server Components too. - Figma: the dark tooltip of the Net Worth card (1473:77748) and the white tooltip of the Finance Overview Area card (1473:75992).

items.title: Chart Trend
items.description: A trend-up / trend-down arrow with the change in green or red and a soft label ("↗ 4.82% this month"); a new value counts from the previous one.

The number is shown without a sign, the arrow says which way; a new value counts from the previous one with anime.js. ## Usage ```tsx import { ChartTrend } from "@/components/ui/chart-trend" export function Example() { return (

items.name: charts-trends-tooltip
items.title: Chart Trends Tooltip
items.description: The content of the Trends cards' tooltip: the date on a grey pill, then a row per series with its 10px legend swatch, its name and the amount (counting to new values with anime.js), the amounts lined up.

meta.docs:
What the tooltip of the Trends cards (Financial Trends, Growth Trends) holds: the date on a Background/Disable pill, then a row per series with its 10px legend swatch, its name and the amount, the names in a column at least 100px wide so the amounts line up. With `counting`, the amounts count from the previous ones with anime.js. It has no box of its own: put it in your tooltip (a column, 8px apart), and render it again without `counting` in an invisible copy to measure the tooltip at its final size while the amounts count. ## Usage ```tsx "use client" import { ChartTrendsTooltipContent, type ChartTrendsTooltipRow } from "@/components/ui/chart-trends-tooltip" import { formatCurrency } from "@/lib/chart-format" const rows: ChartTrendsTooltipRow[] = [ { id: "inflow", label: "Cash inflow", value: 1784.95, swatch: "bg-surface-soft [--swatch-ring:#e5e5e5]" }, { id: "outflow", label: "Cash outflow", value: 2174.64, swatch: "bg-primary-blue-500 [--swatch-ring:var(--primary-blue-500)]" }, ] const money = (value: number) => formatCurrency(value) export function Example() { return (
) } ``` ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `date` | `React.ReactNode` | – | The first line (Label/02 Medium, Text/Loud). | | `rows` | `ChartTrendsTooltipRow[]` | – | `{ id, label, value, swatch }`: `swatch` holds the classes of the row's 10px ChartLegendSwatch (its fill and `--swatch-ring`). | | `format` | `(value: number) => string` | – | The amounts (Label/03 Medium). | | `counting` | `boolean` | `false` | Count the amounts to new values (450ms): on in the tooltip, off in a measured copy. | It renders a fragment. The parts carry `data-slot="chart-trends-tooltip-date"`, `"chart-trends-tooltip-rows"` and, with `counting`, `"chart-trends-tooltip-value"` on each amount (with its number in `data-value`), so an entrance can count them up from zero. ## Notes - The tooltip box in Figma: Background/White, 12px corners, 4px padding, a #f2f2f2 ring and two soft shadows (the classes in the example); the cards position it by the selected column. - Figma: the tooltip 1473:84903 in the Financial Trends card.

items.name: charts-use-chart-size
items.title: useChartSize
items.description: An element's content-box size from a ResizeObserver (callback ref + size, starting at the design size), so line charts draw their paths at the width they get.

meta.docs:
A hook that keeps an element's content-box size from a `ResizeObserver`. It returns a callback ref and the size, which starts at the size you pass (also the server render), so a chart draws at its design size first and redraws at the width it actually gets. The line charts use it to build their paths in pixels. ## Usage ```tsx "use client" import { useChartSize } from "@/hooks/use-chart-size" const values = [40, 72, 56, 88, 64, 96] export function Example() { const [ref, { width, height }] = useChartSize({ width: 320, height: 96 }) const points = values.map((v, i) => `${(i / (values.length - 1)) * width},${height - (v / 100) * height}`).join(" ") return (
) } ``` ## API `useChartSize(initial: { width: number; height: number }) => readonly [(node: T | null) => void, { width: number; height: number }]` ## Notes - Measures the content box (padding excluded); updates only when the size changes. - The ref disconnects its observer when the element unmounts (React 19 callback-ref cleanup).
